positions.title: SoC Design Engineer
positions.description: I contribute to design, validation, and tools/flows/methodologies, leveraging over a decade of experience in the semiconductor industry and a unique grasp of both software engineering and hardware design principles to improve processes and enable the team to do more with less.
positions.insights: Skills: Shell Scripting · TCL · Verdi · Algorithms · GNU Make · Ruby · Formal property verification · Python (Programming Language) · X86 · Git · Bazel · SystemVerilog

positions.title: Design Verification Engineer
positions.description: I develop, maintain, and use custom software written in various languages (C, C++, Ruby, Python, lua, javascript, SystemVerilog, etc.) to fulfill responsibilities in design verification, post-silicon validation, and manufacturing test pattern generation for X86 processor designs. This includes UVM-based unit-level verification test benches, full-chip verification, test pattern generator software development, JTAG/IJTAG software development and hardware verification and debugging, MBIST (Memory Built In Self Test) verification and manufacturing pattern generation, and other internal software and web app development.
positions.insights: Skills: Shell Scripting · TCL · Verdi · Algorithms · GNU Make · Ruby · Python (Programming Language) · Universal Verification Methodology (UVM) · Ruby on Rails · X86 · Git · Bazel · JavaScript · Docker · Lua · SystemVerilog

projects.title: Awesome Ball iPhone app
projects.description:
Originally created as part of a contest at BYU, Awesome Ball was an iPhone app that simulated a ball bouncing in a three-dimensional box inside your phone. It used OpenGL graphics and the ODE physics engine to make a realistic bouncing ball that could be customized to the user's desire.

This was a fun project to do and resulted in over 2 million downloads of the app around the world (mostly free downloads).

The Awesome Ball source code is available on GitHub:
https://github.com/brianpratt/awesomeball
